name: Pt
doc:
A point of `n`-dimensional real space.

This is `Lattice.Core.Syntax.Point` at `R = ℝ`, not a new abbreviation: defining a second `Point` would be
the exact duplication `Core` exists to prevent, and invariant I3 caught an earlier revision doing it.
stmt: abbrev Pt (n : ℕ)

name: GeoExpr
doc:
**Geometric polynomial expressions.**

Atoms are the coordinates of numbered points; the operations are addition, subtraction and
multiplication. There is no `div` and no `sqrt` -- see the module docstring.

The expression depends on `n` (the ambient dimension) but *not* on how many points the configuration
has, so the same constraint can be interpreted in any configuration.
stmt:
inductive GeoExpr (n : ℕ) : Type where
                                                      
  | coord (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n)
                         
  | const (c : ℝ)
  | add (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)
  | sub (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)
  | mul (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)

namespace GeoExpr

variable {n : ℕ}

name: zero
doc: Zero as an expression. Convenient as a right-hand side for "this vanishes".
stmt: def zero : GeoExpr n

name: one
stmt: def one : GeoExpr n

name: evalPts
doc:
**Evaluation** in a configuration, i.e. for a family of points.

The interpretation is a function `ℕ → Pt n`: point index to coordinates. Coordinates are addressed
directly (`pts p axis`), which is what `IRExpr` could not do for the second component.
stmt: noncomputable def evalPts (e : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof:
match e with
  | .coord p axis => pts p axis
  | .const c => c
  | .add e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts + e₂.evalPts pts
  | .sub e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts - e₂.evalPts pts
  | .mul e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts * e₂.evalPts pts

name: evalPts_coord
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_coord (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (coord p axis).evalPts pts = pts p axis

name: evalPts_const
stmt: @[simp] theorem evalPts_const (c : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : (const c).evalPts pts = c

name: evalPts_add
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_add (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.add e₂).evalPts pts = e₁.evalPts pts + e₂.evalPts pts

name: evalPts_sub
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_sub (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.sub e₂).evalPts pts = e₁.evalPts pts - e₂.evalPts pts

name: evalPts_mul
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_mul (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.mul e₂).evalPts pts = e₁.evalPts pts * e₂.evalPts pts

name: evalPts_zero
stmt: @[simp] theorem evalPts_zero (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : (zero : GeoExpr n).evalPts pts = 0

name: evalPts_one
stmt: @[simp] theorem evalPts_one (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : (one : GeoExpr n).evalPts pts = 1

name: evalPts_sub_eq_zero_iff
doc:
The difference of two expressions vanishing is the same as the two values being equal.

This is the form every equality constraint reduces to, and it is `rfl`-adjacent, which is why it is
recorded: `eval a = eval b ↔ eval (sub a b) = 0` is what lets a constraint be turned into a
polynomial whose zero set is the solution set.
stmt:
theorem evalPts_sub_eq_zero_iff (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.sub e₂).evalPts pts = 0 ↔ e₁.evalPts pts = e₂.evalPts pts
proof:
by
  simp [sub_eq_zero]

end GeoExpr

end Lattice.Geo

name: GeoExpr.maxPoint
doc:
**The largest point index an expression mentions.** A carrier with more than this many points can read the
expression; that is exactly the bound the differentiability statement needs.
stmt:
def GeoExpr.maxPoint : GeoExpr n → ℕ
  | .coord p _ => p
  | .const _ => 0
  | .add e₁ e₂ => max (maxPoint e₁) (maxPoint e₂)
  | .sub e₁ e₂ => max (maxPoint e₁) (maxPoint e₂)
  | .mul e₁ e₂ => max (maxPoint e₁) (maxPoint e₂)

name: maxPoint_lt_of_coord
doc:
**A flattened configuration reads every point the expression mentions**, given `maxPoint e < k`.

This is the bridge between the side condition and the carrier: it is what lets each `coord` case of the induction
produce a projection instead of getting stuck.
stmt:
theorem maxPoint_lt_of_coord {e : GeoExpr n} {p : ℕ} {axis : Fin n}
    (h : GeoExpr.coord p axis = e) (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k) : p < k
proof:
by
  subst h
  simpa [GeoExpr.maxPoint] using hk

name: toNatConfig
doc:
**A finite configuration read as an `ℕ`-indexed one**, filling the remaining points with the origin.

The bridge between the flattened carrier (where analysis works) and `evalPts`'s own domain. Points beyond `k`
are never read, because `maxPoint e < k` bounds every index an expression can mention.
stmt: noncomputable def toNatConfig (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) : ℕ → Pt n
proof: fun p => if h : p < k then unflatten w ⟨p, h⟩ else 0

name: derivExpr
doc:
**The derivative of an expression's evaluation, as a continuous linear functional on the flattened carrier.**

Defined by recursion so that `hasFDerivAt_eval` is an induction rather than a definition unfolding. The `mul`
case carries the product rule verbatim, which is why the operator-valued recursion closes.
stmt:
noncomputable def derivExpr (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    (Fin (k * n) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ
proof:
match e with
  | .coord p axis =>
    if h : p < k then coordProj k n ⟨p, h⟩ axis else 0
  | .const _ => 0
  | .add e₁ e₂ => derivExpr k e₁ w + derivExpr k e₂ w
  | .sub e₁ e₂ => derivExpr k e₁ w - derivExpr k e₂ w
  | .mul e₁ e₂ =>
    e₂.evalPts (toNatConfig w) • derivExpr k e₁ w
      + e₁.evalPts (toNatConfig w) • derivExpr k e₂ w

name: maxPoint_le_add_left
doc: **Every subexpression's points are within the whole's bound.**
stmt: theorem maxPoint_le_add_left {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.add e₁ e₂)

name: maxPoint_le_sub_left
stmt: theorem maxPoint_le_sub_left {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.sub e₁ e₂)

name: maxPoint_le_mul_left
stmt: theorem maxPoint_le_mul_left {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.mul e₁ e₂)

name: lt_of_le_maxPoint
doc: **A point index below the whole's bound is below `k`.**
stmt:
theorem lt_of_le_maxPoint {e : GeoExpr n} {p : ℕ} (h : p ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint e)
    (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k) : p < k

name: maxPoint_lt_of_le
doc: **A subexpression's bound follows from the whole's.**
stmt:
theorem maxPoint_lt_of_le {e : GeoExpr n} {p : ℕ} (hp : p ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint e)
    (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k) : p < k

name: evalPts_coord_of_lt
doc:
**A configuration reads a coordinate the same way on both carriers.**

The link between `evalPts` (on `ℕ → Pt n`) and `unflatten` (on the flattened carrier): for a point index within
the bound, the two agree.
proof:
by
  show toNatConfig w p axis = unflatten w ⟨p, hpk⟩ axis
  unfold toNatConfig
  rw [dif_pos hpk]

name: hasFDerivAt_eval
doc:
**Every expression is differentiable on a carrier large enough to read it.**

The bound `maxPoint e < k` is the content of "large enough": an expression mentioning point `k` has no place to
live on a carrier with `k` points, and the `coord` case would have to produce a projection for a point that does
not exist.

The induction is structural. `coord` cites `Lattice.Geo.Differentiable.hasFDerivAt_coord`; `const` is constant;
`add` and `sub` combine by linearity; `mul` uses the product rule with the subexpressions' values as
coefficients, which are themselves differentiable by the induction hypotheses.
stmt:
theorem hasFDerivAt_eval (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k)
    (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) (derivExpr k e w) w
proof:
by
  induction e with
  | coord p axis =>
                                                                           
    by_cases hpk : p < k
    · have := hasFDerivAt_coord (k := k) (n := n) ⟨p, hpk⟩ axis w
                                                                                                
      simpa [derivExpr, dif_pos hpk, toNatConfig, dif_pos hpk] using this
    · exact absurd (lt_of_le_of_lt (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] : p ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.coord p axis)) hk) hpk
  | const c =>
                                     
    simpa [derivExpr] using
      (hasFDerivAt_const (c : ℝ) (x := w) : HasFDerivAt (fun _ : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => c) 0 w)
  | add e₁ e₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    have h₁ := ih₁ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    have h₂ := ih₂ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    simpa [derivExpr, GeoExpr.evalPts] using h₁.add h₂
  | sub e₁ e₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    have h₁ := ih₁ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    have h₂ := ih₂ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    simpa [derivExpr, GeoExpr.evalPts] using h₁.sub h₂
  | mul e₁ e₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    have hk₁ : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ < k := by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega
    have hk₂ : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₂ < k := by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega
    have h₁ := ih₁ hk₁
    have h₂ := ih₂ hk₂
                                                                                               
    have hmul := h₁.mul h₂
    simpa [derivExpr, GeoExpr.evalPts, smul_eq_mul, add_comm]

name: evalPts_hasNonzeroDeriv
doc:
**A non-vanishing derivative of `evalPts` is exactly `HasNonzeroDeriv`**, because `hasFDerivAt_eval` already
supplies the `HasFDerivAt` half with `derivExpr k e w` as the derivative.
stmt:
theorem evalPts_hasNonzeroDeriv
    (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (hk : e.maxPoint < k) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ)
    (hne : derivExpr k e w ≠ 0) :
    HasNonzeroDeriv (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) w
proof: ⟨derivExpr k e w, hne, hasFDerivAt_eval k e hk w⟩

name: evalPts_localMin_implies_zero
doc:
**The expression penalty's local-minimum guarantee.**

With the derivative non-vanishing, a local minimum of the squared penalty forces the penalty to vanish -- so the
configuration satisfies the expression equation exactly. Without that hypothesis the statement is false: a constant
expression minimizes its own penalty everywhere and equals its constant, which need not be zero.

The two halves come from the two modules: `hasFDerivAt_eval` (differentiation) and `localMin_implies_zero`
(first-order optimality).
stmt:
theorem evalPts_localMin_implies_zero
    (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (hk : e.maxPoint < k) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ)
    (hne : derivExpr k e w ≠ 0)
    (hmin : IsLocalMin
      (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => (e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) ^ 2) w) :
    e.evalPts (toNatConfig w) = 0
proof:
localMin_implies_zero (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) w
    (evalPts_hasNonzeroDeriv k e hk w hne) hmin

name: constExpr_localMin_counterexample
doc:
**A constant expression is the counterexample the hypothesis excludes**, stated so the boundary above is not
merely asserted: every point is a local minimum of its squared penalty, and the penalty equals the constant
everywhere rather than vanishing.
stmt:
theorem constExpr_localMin_counterexample
    (c : ℝ) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    IsLocalMin (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => ((GeoExpr.const c).evalPts (toNatConfig y)) ^ 2) w
proof:
by
  have hconst : ∀ y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ, (GeoExpr.const c).evalPts (toNatConfig y) = c := by
    intro y
    simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]
  simp only [hconst]
  exact isLocalMin_const

end Lattice.Geo
